Thought Process
To find the maximum of a circular linked list, follow the approach below.
1. Create a tracking pointer
To track our current position in the list, we create a pointer current. Initially current is the head.
Node<T>* current = head;
2. Assume head has the maximum value.
To get the largest value in a linked list we have to compare the value of each node with the largest value among all its preceding nodes.
Initially we have no value to compare with so we assume that the head has the largest value.
int maximum = head->data;
3. Compare node value with the current maximum value.
We then check to see if the current node value is greater than the current largest value. If it is, assign the largest with the current node value.
4. Repeat the process until you reach the head node again.
We traverse through the entire list and perform step 3 for every node we visit.
